raised: Nothing on the page helps a 61-year-old decide whether a 99%-stock track suits them (no guidance by age)
The opening bullets speak to the designers, not to the user
The 'מקום' tab means nothing to the user
Several of the investment-type filter buttons are confusing
The orange note in option A shows most groups are cut off, including the bond groups the user wants
Option B mixes bonds, stocks and cash in one fee-sorted list, which makes comparison meaningless
The clock icons and dotted purple underlines are unexplained
Doesn't understand what 'מט"ח 97%' means for them
Doesn't understand how shares can be 'מניות 101%'
Can't tell the investment groups apart ('מניות', 'מניות סחיר', 'עוקב מדדי מניות', 'גמיש', 'משולב סחיר', 'קיימות')
Unclear whether 'מההפקדות' means a fee on every deposit
Unclear how much is actually kept once returns are shown before fees and before tax
Unclear whether a 'פחות מ־3 שנים' track is riskier or just new
No risk information, such as how far a track fell in a bad year
Option C shows returns only for the S&P group, not for bonds or the general track
No practical rules on switching tracks or on tax at withdrawal
No information on how to actually join
The 'קופה' code column is meaningless and could go
The ring charts repeat the percentages and could go
The tabs and product buttons repeated above each option could go

problems.why: The report never says the lists fail to show how the companies differ. It only notes that the company choice hardly matters because returns are close, which is a different point.

The "קופה" column is just an unexplained code

Unclear how "מניות 101%" can be over 100%
The differences between groups such as מניות, מניות סחיר, עוקב מדדי מניות, גמיש, משולב סחיר and קיימות are unclear
Unclear whether "מההפקדות" means a fee on every deposit
Returns are shown before fees and tax, so the reader can't tell what they actually keep
Unclear whether "פחות מ־3 שנים" means riskier or just new
No risk information, such as how far a track fell in a bad year
